seam.definition: The line where two pieces of fabric are sewn together.

dart.definition: A tapered fold sewn into fabric to shape a garment.

pleat.definition: A fold pressed or sewn into fabric.

gather.definition: To draw fabric together into small folds with stitches.

hem.definition: The edge of a piece of cloth.

collar.definition: The part of a garment that surrounds the neck.

cuff.definition: The finished band or edge at the end of a sleeve.

sleeve.definition: The part of a garment that is attached at the armhole and that provides a cloth covering for the arm.

bodice.definition: Part of a dress above the waist.

waistband.definition: A band of material around the waist that strengthens a skirt or trousers.

zipper.definition: A fastener with two rows of teeth that join when a slider moves along them.

button.definition: A small fastener attached to clothing and passed through a buttonhole.

snap.definition: A clothing fastener made from two parts that press together.

hook-and-eye.definition: A clothing fastener made from a small hook that catches on a matching loop.

velcro.definition: A hook-and-loop fastener used to join two surfaces.

buckle.definition: A frame-and-pin fastener used to secure a belt or strap.

lace-up.definition: Fastened or decorated with laces threaded through holes or loops.
lace-up.exampleUsage: The design uses a lace-up front.

toggle.definition: A fastener consisting of a peg or pin or crosspiece that is inserted into an eye at the end of a rope or a chain or a cable in order to fasten it to something (as another rope or chain or cable).

drawstring.definition: A tie consisting of a cord that goes through a seam around an opening.

magnetic-clasp.definition: A fastener that uses magnets to hold two parts together.
magnetic-clasp.exampleUsage: The bag closes with a magnetic clasp.

embroidery.definition: Decorative designs stitched onto fabric with thread.

beading.definition: Decoration made by attaching small beads to fabric.

sequin.definition: Adornment consisting of a small piece of shiny material used to decorate clothing.

appliqu-.definition: A decorative technique in which pieces of fabric are attached onto a larger fabric surface to form shapes or patterns.
appliqu-.exampleUsage: The designer added floral appliqué to the sample.

fringe.definition: A row of hanging threads or strips along an edge.

ruffle.definition: A gathered strip of fabric used as decoration.

ribbon.definition: A narrow strip of fabric used for decoration or fastening.

piping.definition: A narrow strip of fabric sewn into an edge or seam for decoration.

smocking.definition: Embroidery consisting of ornamental needlework on a garment that is made by gathering the cloth tightly in stitches.

monogram.definition: A graphic symbol consisting of 2 or more letters combined (usually your initials).

haute-couture.definition: High-end fashion made to an individual customer's measurements.

pr-t-porter.definition: A French fashion term meaning ready-to-wear clothing produced in standard sizes rather than custom-made for one person.
pr-t-porter.exampleUsage: The collection was presented as prêt-à-porter.

collection.definition: A coordinated group of garments created by a designer or brand.

season.definition: A fashion-design and sales period, such as spring/summer or autumn/winter.

lookbook.definition: A collection of photographs or illustrations showing a designer's clothing, products, or visual style.
lookbook.exampleUsage: The brand released a lookbook for the new collection.

trend.definition: A general direction in which something tends to move.

silhouette.definition: The overall outline or shape of a garment.

colorway.definition: A particular combination or arrangement of colors used in a design or product.
colorway.exampleUsage: The shoe is available in a second colorway.

capsule.definition: A small coordinated collection of clothing pieces that work together.

sustainable-fashion.definition: An approach to clothing design and production that aims to reduce environmental harm and improve social responsibility across the product life cycle.
sustainable-fashion.exampleUsage: The class discussed material choices in sustainable fashion.
